title: BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective F may be nonconvex. Its gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, and some lower bound a satisfies F(x₀) − a ≤ Δ. Each local function is differentiable. The smoothness bound applies to the aggregate gradient.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n) Σᵢ fᵢ(x), with one local function per worker. The local gradients may differ arbitrarily at a common point.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query (x,m) at worker i requests m ≥ 1 fresh gradients at x. The reply contains all m vectors. Each sample has mean ∇fᵢ(x).
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, ComputeQuery, ComputeReply, computation and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.unbiased

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The communication oracle transports finite bit strings between any ordered pair of workers. The receiver observes the sender and the delivered bits.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every i and x, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − ∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σ². Samples are IID within each worker under its own law μᵢ, and the entire sample streams are independent across workers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Query points, local gradient samples and the output belong to Euclidean ℝᵈ.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.d and Point. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, Point, ComputeReply and spec.Output

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Worker i takes m hᵢ time for a batch of size m and can have one batch pending. A k-bit payload occupies its directed link for ℓ + b(k + 64) time, including the 64-bit trailer. Messages queue in submission order on each link. Distinct links and workers can operate concurrently. All parameters are public, including hᵢ > 0, ℓ,b ≥ 0, L > 0, Δ,σ ≥ 0, ε > 0, n, d and x₀. The local functions, gradient maps and sampling laws are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, computation, communication, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits and step

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The designated root returns one measurable point X by the elapsed-time deadline. The squared Euclidean norm of the aggregate gradient at X must be integrable.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.Output and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E‖∇F(X)‖² ≤ ε² under the product law of the algorithm and oracle seeds. Execution must also have finitely many events almost surely through the specified deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents and TimedConvergence

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The elapsed-time guarantee couples heterogeneous local sampling times with concurrent, queued, finite-bit communication. Both the number of messages on a link and their encoded lengths affect when the root can return its point.

descriptionHtml:
Bandwidth-Limited Distributed Nonconvex Optimization

We seek a stationary point of a possibly nonconvex objective f on Rd, where d≥0 is the dimension. The objective averages differentiable worker functions, has a Lipschitz gradient, and admits a lower bound with a prescribed gap from the initial value. Each worker returns a batch of unbiased local gradient estimates with bounded variance, using independent samples within and across workers. Workers have heterogeneous computation times and communicate over directed links with latency and per-bit costs. For tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯ satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥2≤ε2, averaging over sampling and algorithm randomness.

With n≥1 workers and local functions fi:Rd→R, the optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x),f(x)=1n∑i=1nfi(x). All norms are Euclidean. The algorithm receives d, n, the measurable sample space Ω, the starting point x0∈Rd, the smoothness constant L>0, the initial gap bound Δ≥0, the noise bound σ≥0, the tolerance ε, the worker computation times hi>0, the link latency ℓ≥0, and the transmission time per bit b≥0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Aggregate smoothness and initial gap). Each fi is differentiable on Rd. There exists a∈R such that, for all x,y∈Rd, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,a≤f(x),f(x0)−a≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Local stochastic gradients). Worker i has a sequence (ξi,k)k≥0 of independent measurable samples with common law μi on Ω. The worker sequences are mutually independent, and the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample array. Each map gi:Rd×Ω→Rd is jointly measurable. For every x∈Rd and ξ∼μi, the vector gi(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable, its squared error is integrable, and Eξ∼μi[gi(x,ξ)]=∇fi(x),Eξ∼μi[∥gi(x,ξ)−∇fi(x)∥2]≤σ2.

An idle worker i accepts a query consisting of a point x∈Rd and an integer batch size m≥1. After mhi units of time it returns the ordered list (gi(x,ξi,k),…,gi(x,ξi,k+m−1)), where k is the number of samples already used by that worker. A worker ignores further computation requests while its batch is pending. Different workers may compute concurrently.

Every ordered pair of workers, including a worker paired with itself, has a directed link. Messages on each link are queued in submission order. A message submitted at time t with a payload of q≥0 bits is ready for delivery at time max{t,c}+ℓ+b(q+64), where c is the completion time of the preceding message on that link, or zero for the first message. The receiver obtains the sender’s identity and the payload followed by the 64 zero bits included in the transmission cost. Distinct directed links may transmit concurrently, and communication may overlap computation.

For an elapsed-time budget T≥0, almost surely every deadline s∈[0,T] must be reached with only finitely many events through that deadline. At time T, the algorithm’s designated root worker must produce a measurable output x¯∈Rd with integrable squared gradient norm satisfying E[∥∇f(x¯)∥2]≤ε2.

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, F=n−1∑ifi has L-Lipschitz gradient and F(x0)−infF≤Δ. The fi are differentiable and their gradients may differ arbitrarily. Jointly measurable local oracles are unbiased with variance at most σ2. Samples are IID within each worker and independent across workers. Worker i processes one batch at a time at hi>0 per sample. Each ordered pair has a separate FIFO link. Links operate concurrently with each other and with computation. A B-bit packet including its header takes ℓ+bB time. For n≥1, L,ε>0 and Δ,σ,ℓ,b≥0, the target is a measurable output X with E∥∇F(X)∥2≤ε2 under the execution law.

Elapsed-time upper bounds for smooth nonconvex optimization with heterogeneous workers and finite-bit links.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) FiniteBitLeon (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(K[C+ℓ+b(1+mlog⁡(2+nd))])
(2) Derived bound: full-range modulus (LongTails 2026) O(K[C+ℓ+b(1+mlog⁡(2+nd+K))]) (1): Multiscale anchors remove K from the packet-size logarithm. For σ=cε and other parameters fixed and positive (n≥2, d≥1), total time falls from O(ε−2log⁡(1/ε)) to O(ε−2) as ε→0. Sampling or latency can mask the gain. (1) stores leaf iterates and maintains a tree of anchors.
(3) Leon SGD (Tyurin 2026, Thm. 1.7) O(K[C+τd/(n−1)]) on a complete graph, n≥2, with zero latency and exact real coordinates. (1) preserves the sampling-time dependence using finite binary packets and accounts for latency. The different transmission units preclude a total-time comparison. (1) requires a complete multiport network and has large constants. (3) allows general connected bidirectional graphs.

import LongTails.Setups.DistributedSmoothNonconvex
import LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex

open DistributedTemplate
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticSmoothAndConvex (IsStochasticGradient)
open LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex (IID)

abbrev Params := DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Params
abbrev Point := DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Point
abbrev Samples := DistributedSmoothNonconvex.Samples
abbrev Functions (p : Params) := Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ
abbrev ComputeQuery (p : Params) := Point p × ℕ+
abbrev ComputeReply (p : Params) := List (Point p)
abbrev CommReply (p : Params) := Fin p.n × List Bool

noncomputable def objective (p : Params) (f : Functions p) : Point p → ℝ :=
  FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective f

structure ComputeState (p : Params) where
  samples : Samples p
  used : ℕ
  pending : Option (Time × ComputeQuery p)

noncomputable def computation (p : Params) (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p) :
    ComputationOracle (ComputeQuery p) (ComputeReply p) (Samples p) p.n where
  State := ComputeState p
  initial _ s := ⟨s, 0, none⟩
  submit i s t q :=
    if s.pending.isSome then s else { s with pending := some (t + (q.2 : ℕ) * p.h i, q) }
  answer i s t := do
    let (finish, x, m) ← s.pending
    if finish ≤ t then
      return ((List.range m).map (fun j => g i x (s.samples i (s.used + j))),
        { s with used := s.used + m, pending := none })
    else none

abbrev Mail (p : Params) := Fin p.n × Fin p.n → List (Time × List Bool)

noncomputable def communication (p : Params) :
    CommunicationOracle (CommReply p) (Samples p) p.n where
  State := Mail p
  initial _ := fun _ => []
  submit s t i q :=
    let edge := (i, q.1)
    let start := max t (((s edge).getLast?.map Prod.fst).getD 0)
    Function.update s edge (s edge ++ [(start + p.l + p.b * q.2.length, q.2)])
  answer s t := by
    classical
    exact if h : ∃ edge : Fin p.n × Fin p.n, ∃ m ∈ (s edge).head?, m.1 ≤ t then
      let e := h.choose
      let m := h.choose_spec.choose
      some ((e.2, (e.1, m.2)), Function.update s e (s e).tail)
    else none

noncomputable def system (p : Params) (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)) :
    Oracle (ComputeQuery p) (ComputeReply p) (CommReply p) p.n where
  Seed := Samples p
  law := P
  computation := computation p g
  communication := communication p

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  numWorkers p := p.n
  Instance := Functions
  ComputeQuery := ComputeQuery
  ComputeReply := ComputeReply
  CommReply := CommReply
  Output := Point
  publicInput := id
  valid p := (∀ i, 0 < p.h i) ∧ 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient (objective p f) x - gradient (objective p f) y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ a : ℝ, (∀ x, a ≤ objective p f x) ∧ objective p f p.x0 - a ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ (g : Fin p.n → Point p → p.Ω → Point p)
      (μ : Fin p.n → ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (Samples p)),
      O = system p g P ∧
      ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i (s : Samples p) => s i) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∀ i, IID (fun k (s : Samples p) => s i k) (μ i : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
        IsStochasticGradient (Point p) p.Ω (μ i) (f i) (g i) p.σ
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient (objective p f) (output ω)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, ‖gradient (objective p f) (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex
